questions.question: The surface area of a sphere Is 5544 cm². If the radius of the sphere is doubled, then find the surface area of the new sphere (in cm²).
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **surface area** of a **sphere** is proportional to the square of its **radius** (Area ∝ r²).

If the **radius** is **doubled** (becomes 2 times), the **new surface area** becomes 2² = 4 times the original area.

New Surface Area = 4 × 5544 = 22,176 cm².

**∴ The correct answer is 22,176 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Original **Surface Area** (A₁) = 5544 cm²

**Formula Used:**

**Surface Area** of **sphere** = 4πr²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ec96920336bd7c48cb30446c3aa808b27128ec414e751b2ee32734268883c52f.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ A₁ = 4πr² = 5544

⇒ Let the **new radius** be R = 2r.

⇒ New **Surface Area** (A₂) = 4πR²

⇒ A₂ = 4π(2r)²

⇒ A₂ = 4π(4r²)

⇒ A₂ = 4 × (4πr²)

⇒ Substituting the value of 4πr²:

⇒ A₂ = 4 × 5544

⇒ A₂ = 22,176 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 22,176 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Volume of a Sphere

The volume (V) of a **sphere** is given by V = (4/3)πr³. If the **radius** is doubled, the **volume** increases by 2³ = 8 times.

Surface Area of Hemisphere

For a **hemisphere** of **radius** r, the **curved surface area** is 2πr² and the **total surface area** is 3πr².

Ratio Property

For any two **spheres** with radii r₁ and r₂, the **ratio of their surface areas** is (r₁/r₂)² and the **ratio of their volumes** is (r₁/r₂)³.</p

questions.question: A sailor rows a boat 36 km downstream and 24 km upstream in 6 hours. When it rows 24 km downstream and 36 km upstream the sailor takes 6 and half hours. Then the speed of the current is:
questions.solution:
Given:

Distance downstream in first case = 36 km.

Distance upstream in first case = 24 km.

Time for first case = 6 hours.

Distance downstream in second case = 24 km.

Distance upstream in second case = 36 km.

Time for second case = 6.5 hours.

Formula Used:

Speed = Distance / Time

Let the speed of the boat in still water be b

Upstream speed = b - cb - c

Time = Distance / Speed

Calculation:

For the first case:

36/(b + c) + 24/(b - c) = 6

For the second case:

24/(b + c) + 36/(b - c) = 6.5 

Let's solve these two equations to find the value of b and c:-

Let 1/(b + c) = x and 1/(b - c) = y

From the first case:

36/(b + c) + 24/(b − c) = 6 

⇒ 36x + 24y = 6 ...(1)

From the second case:

24/(b + c) + 36/(b − c) = 6.5

⇒ 24x + 36y = 6.5 ...(2)

On solving (1) and (2):-

y = 1/8

so

b - c = 8

and

x = 1/12

b + c = 12

so, b = 10 km/hr and c = 2 km/hr

**​The speed of the stream is 2 km/hr.**

questions.question: From a cuboid of dimension of 8 × 6 × 6 units. small cubes of dimension 0.5 × 0.5 × 0.5 unit are cut. How many small cubes can be cut from the big cuboid?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Number of cubes along length = 8 ÷ 0.5 = 16

Number of cubes along width & height = 6 ÷ 0.5 = 12

⇒ Total small cubes = 16 × 12 × 12 = 2304

**∴ The correct answer is 2304 cubes.**

**__Alternate Method__**

Dimensions of the big cuboid = 8 units × 6 units × 6 units

Dimension of a small cube = 0.5 unit × 0.5 unit × 0.5 unit

**Formula Used:**

Volume of Cuboid = Length × Width × Height

Volume of Cube = Side × Side × Side

Number of cubes = Volume of big cuboid ÷ Volume of small cube

**Calculation:**

⇒ Volume of the big cuboid = 8 × 6 × 6 = 288 cubic units

⇒ Volume of a small cube = 0.5 × 0.5 × 0.5 = 0.125 cubic units

⇒ Number of small cubes = 288 ÷ 0.125

⇒ Number of small cubes = (288 × 1000) ÷ 125 = 2304

**∴ The correct answer is 2304 cubes.**

questions.question: From a container having pure milk, 35% is replaced by water and the process is repeated thrice. At the end of the third operation. the purity of the milk is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Milk **Final Concentration** = Initial Concentration × (1 − Replacement Fraction)ⁿ

Replacement fraction = 35% = 35/100 = 7/20

Remaining fraction per operation = 1 − 7/20 = 13/20

After 3 operations, Purity = 100% × (13/20)³ = 100% × (2197/8000) = 2197/80 %

2197/80 = 27 (37/80) %

**∴ The correct answer is 27(37)/(80)%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Initial purity of milk = 100%. Replacement percentage = 35% each time. Number of operations (n) = 3.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d1aef5690f353d2d7e6237e87a37655c5a7fb1c508138a8dec0c6e0b713e7009.png] 

**Formula:** Final Quantity = Initial Quantity × (1 − x/V)ⁿ

⇒ Let **Initial Quantity** of pure milk be 100 units.

⇒ Milk after 1st operation = 100 × (1 − 35/100) = 100 × 65/100 = 65 units.

⇒ Milk after 2nd operation = 65 × (1 − 35/100) = 65 × 13/20 = 845/20 = 42.25 units.

⇒ Milk after 3rd operation = 42.25 × (13/20) = 549.25/20 = 27.4625 units.

⇒ In fraction form: 100 × (13/20) × (13/20) × (13/20) = 100 × (2197/8000)

⇒ Final Purity = 2197/80 % = 27 (37/80) %

**∴ The correct answer is 27(37)/(80)%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Repeated Replacement Formula

When a certain quantity 'x' is removed from total volume 'V' and replaced by another liquid 'n' times, the **Final Liquid Quantity** = V × (1 − x/V)ⁿ.

Ratio of Milk and Water

The ratio of **Milk to Water** after n operations is [V(1 − x/V)ⁿ] : [V − V(1 − x/V)ⁿ].

Successive Percentage Change

This problem is a case of **Successive Percentage Decrease**, similar to the **Depreciation** formula in Compound Interest.</p

questions.question: The income of X is 12% more than that of Y. By how much per cent is Y's income less than that of X?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If A is R% more than B, then B is less than A by directly using the formula: [R ÷ (100 + R)] × 100%

⇒ Here, X is 12% more than Y, so R = 12

⇒ Required percentage = [12 ÷ (100 + 12)] × 100%

⇒ Required percentage = (12 ÷ 112) × 100%

⇒ Required percentage = (3 ÷ 28) × 100% = 300 ÷ 28 = 75 ÷ 7 = 10 ⁵/₇%

**∴ The correct answer is 10 ⁵/₇%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b5fc3720b3b8c6eec45f9760bc67cf5bf3c19e442862e4bd2e0a50d2bd2b4471.png] 

**Given:**

⇒ The income of X is 12% more than that of Y.

**Formula Used:**

⇒ Percentage Less = [Difference ÷ Reference Base] × 100%

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the income of Y be 100 units.

⇒ Then, the income of X = 100 + 12% of 100 = 112 units.

⇒ Difference in their incomes = 112 − 100 = 12 units.

⇒ We need to find by what percentage Y's income is less than X's income. Here, the reference base is X's income.

⇒ Required percentage = (Difference ÷ Income of X) × 100%

⇒ Required percentage = (12 ÷ 112) × 100%

⇒ Required percentage = (3 ÷ 28) × 100%

⇒ Required percentage = 300 ÷ 28 = 75 ÷ 7

⇒ 75 ÷ 7 = 10 with a remainder of 5, which gives 10 ⁵/₇%.

**∴ The correct answer is 10 ⁵/₇%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

AB Rule in Percentage

If A is R% more than B, then B is [R ÷ (100 + R)] × 100% less than A. Conversely, if A is R% less than B, then B is [R ÷ (100 − R)] × 100% more than A.

Percentage Change and Difference

Percentage change heavily depends on the reference base value. The expression (A − B) ÷ B gives how much A is larger than B, whereas (A − B) ÷ A tells how much B is smaller than A.

Successive Percentage Formula

When a value experiences multiple percentage changes successively (x% and y%), the effective net percentage change is given by the formula: x + y + (x × y) ÷ 100.
</p

questions.question: How many kilograms of sugar at Rs. 3.80 per kg must be mixed with 60 kg of sugar at Rs. 4.60 per kg, so that by selling the mixture at Rs. 5.20 per kg there may be a gain of 30%?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Cost price of sugar per kg to be mixed = Rs. 3.80.

Cost price of 60kg of sugar = Rs. 4.60 per kg.

Selling price of the mixture = Rs. 5.20 per kg.

Profit = 30%.

**Formula Used:**

Let the cost price of the mixture per kg be Rs. C.

Profit = (Selling Price - Cost Price) / Cost Price × 100

Weighted Average Cost Price = (Quantity1 × Price1 + Quantity2 × Price2) / (Quantity1 + Quantity2)

**Calculation:**

Let the mass of the sugar to be mixed be x kg.

Cost Price of x kg of sugar at Rs. 3.80 per kg = 3.80x.

Cost Price of 60 kg of sugar at Rs. 4.60 per kg = 4.60 × 60.

⇒ Total Cost Price = 3.80x + 4.60 × 60

⇒ Total Weight = x + 60 kg

Let C be the cost price of the mixture per kg, then

⇒ C = (3.80x + 4.60 × 60) / (x + 60)

Selling price of the mixture = Rs. 5.20 per kg, and profit = 30%,

⇒ C × 1.30 = 5.20

⇒ C = 5.20 / 1.30

⇒ C = 4

Substitute the value of C in the weighted average equation:

⇒ 4 = (3.80x + 276) / (x + 60)

⇒ 4x + 240 = 3.80x + 276

⇒ 4x - 3.80x = 276 - 240

⇒ 0.20x = 36

⇒ x = 36 / 0.20

⇒ x = 180 kg

**Therefore, 180 kg of sugar at Rs. 3.80 per kg must be mixed with 60 kg of sugar at Rs. 4.60 per kg.**

questions.question: A and B can do a piece of work in 9 and 18 days, respectively. They started working together. After some days A left the work and B finished the remaining work in 15 days. After how many days did A leave?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A can do a piece of work in 9 days.

B can do the same piece of work in 18 days.

B finished the remaining work in 15 days after A left.

**Formula Used:**

Work done by A in 1 day = 1/9

Work done by B in 1 day = 1/18

Work done by A and B together in 1 day = Work done by A in 1 day + Work done by B in 1 day

**Calculation:**

Work done by B in 15 days = 15 × 1/18

⇒ Work done by B in 15 days = 15/18

⇒ Work done by B in 15 days = 5/6

Total work - Work done by B in 15 days = Remaining work that was done by A and B together

⇒ 1 - 5/6 = 1/6

Let the number of days A and B worked together be x days.

Work done by A and B together in 1 day = 1/9 + 1/18 = 2/18 + 1/18 = 3/18 = 1/6

So, x × 1/6 = 1/6

⇒ x = 1

**A left the work after 1 day.**

questions.question: The cost price of an article is Rs. 1,120. After allowing a discount of Rs. 205 a gain of 15% was made, then the marked price of the article is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Marked Price (MP) can be calculated directly by adding Profit and Discount to the Cost Price (CP).

MP = CP + Profit + Discount

Profit = 15% of 1120 = Rs. 168

MP = 1120 + 168 + 205 = 1493

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 1,493.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cost Price (CP) = Rs. 1,120

Discount = Rs. 205

Gain = 15%

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = CP + (Gain % of CP)

Marked Price (MP) = SP + Discount

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/507e5f99d3580ffeaf0a00688c06099f1292becb1710bfed4344c1a2ee55ed48.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Profit = 15% of 1120

⇒ Profit = (15 ÷ 100) × 1120 = Rs. 168

⇒ SP = CP + Profit

⇒ SP = 1120 + 168 = Rs. 1288

⇒ MP = SP + Discount

⇒ MP = 1288 + 205 = Rs. 1493

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 1,493.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is always given on the Marked Price (MP) or List Price of an article. Formula: Selling Price = Marked Price − Discount.

Profit & Loss

Profit or Loss is always calculated on the Cost Price (CP) unless stated otherwise. Formula: Selling Price = Cost Price + Profit (or − Loss).

Relationship between MP and CP

A direct proportional relationship exists between MP and CP given by: MP ÷ CP = (100 + Profit%) ÷ (100 − Discount%).
</p

questions.question: If 7 N force is applied on a brick and it moves through 5 m, then what will be the work done?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**35 J**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Work is calculated using the formula: **Work = Force × Displacement × cos(θ)**, where θ is the angle between the force and displacement.
 
• Here, the force applied is **7 N**, and the displacement is **5 m**.
 
• If the force and displacement are in the same direction, cos(θ) = cos(0°) = 1.
 
• Thus, Work = 7 × 5 × 1 = **35 J**.
 
• The unit of work in the SI system is the **joule (J)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Work:**

 
 
• Work is done when a force is applied to an object, and the object moves in the direction of the force.
 
• It is a scalar quantity, meaning it has magnitude but no direction.
 
• The formula for work (W) is **W = F × d × cos(θ)**, where:
 
 
• F = Force applied (N)
 
• d = Displacement (m)
 
• θ = Angle between the force and displacement
 
 
 
 
 
• **Joule:**
 
 
• The joule (J) is the SI unit of work and energy.
 
• **1 joule is equivalent to 1 newton-meter (N·m)**.
 
• It represents the work done when a force of 1 newton displaces an object by 1 meter in the direction of the force.
 
 
 
• **Factors Affecting Work:**
 
 
• The magnitude of the force applied.
 
• The displacement caused by the force.
 
• The angle between the force and the displacement.
 
 
 
• **Work in Different Systems:**
 
 
• In the CGS system, the unit of work is the erg.
 
• **1 erg = 10⁻⁷ joules.**

__
 
• **Budget deficit** occurs when a government spends more money than it receives in revenue.
 
• This usually results in the government having to borrow money to cover the shortfall.
 
• A persistent budget deficit can lead to an increase in public debt.
 
• Managing a budget deficit often involves either increasing revenue (e.g., through taxes) or cutting expenditures.

 Term

 Revenue Deficit

 Primary Deficit

questions.solution:
